identity.title: TileLang: Bridge Programmability and Performance in Modern Neural Kernels

problem.claim: Implementing fused neural kernels for modern AI algorithms is complex.

gap.claim: Existing compilers such as Triton lack fine-grained control needed for kernel implementation.

contributions.claim: Introduces TileLang, a controllable programming system for fused neural kernels with explicit tile-level primitives for memory placement, data movement, and parallel scheduling.
Adds tile inference, which models tile programs as fused graphs and derives tile configurations from partial annotations, plus tile recommendation based on hardware profiles and heuristics.
Reports compact expression of diverse fused attention kernels and performance gains over Triton across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish TileLang through controllable tile-level programming together with tile inference and hardware-aware tile recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that fused attention kernels can be expressed in under 80 lines of Python, with code size reduced by up to 90% versus manual implementations.
The authors report up to 5× speedup over Triton on NVIDIA H100 and up to 6× on AMD GPUs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fused kernels are increasingly used for performance, but existing compilers provide insufficient fine-grained control.
TileLang is introduced as a controllable system with explicit tile-level operations for fused neural kernels.
Tile inference and tile recommendation provide automatic configuration inference and hardware-aware configuration suggestions.
The authors report concise fused-attention implementations and substantial speedups over Triton on NVIDIA and AMD hardware.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs explicit low-level control with automation that infers or recommends tile configurations.

lessons.interpretation: A systems paper can frame programmability and performance as complementary by assigning each to a distinct mechanism.
lessons.application: When proposing a programmable optimization system, separate user-facing control primitives from automated hardware-aware configuration support.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the target workload or hardware does not expose meaningful tile-level configuration choices.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated workloads, exact baselines beyond Triton, measurement methodology, or whether the reported speedups apply broadly across kernels and hardware.
The abstract does not provide details needed to assess the coverage of fused attention kernels or the conditions behind the code-size reductions.
